name: Name
agentOptionalHint: Optional. Without an agent this connection only holds the token, the address and the write mode for your chats. It answers no messages and listens for nothing.
title: PiKVM
intro: Let your chats and agents check a PiKVM and the machine it controls. If you allow it, they can also press its power buttons and use its keyboard, and a person confirms every one of those actions.
limits: An agent that can press a power button or type on a real machine can lose work or run commands. Every action waits for your confirmation. Typing and the hard power actions are off until an administrator switches them on, below. A PiKVM has no user rights: any user it knows can do everything, so the limits of this add-on are the only ones.
userHelp: A dedicated user for LocalAI, so you can remove it later without touching your own login. It is kept sealed with the password and never shown again.
passwdHelp: The password of that user. A PiKVM with two-factor login (2FA) turned on is not supported yet. The user and the password are saved together as user:password, split at the first colon.
userColon: A user name has no colon. The password may have colons.
credControl: The user and the password have no control characters.
credSpace: Remove the spaces around the user or the password.
credLong: The user and the password are too long.
addressHelp: Where you open the PiKVM in a browser, for example https://pikvm.local. For its self-signed certificate add the pin: https://pikvm.local#sha256=<64 hex digits>. One connection is one device. Any other address is refused.
addressShape: This is not an address. Write it as https://name or https://name#sha256=...
addressHttp: Plain http is accepted only for an address on your own network. Use https for anything else.
pinShape: The fingerprint is 64 hexadecimal digits (SHA-256), with or without colons.
pinHttp: A fingerprint goes with an https address.
pinHint: A PiKVM normally has a self-signed certificate. Without a fingerprint pin the Test will say the certificate is not trusted. Add #sha256= and the fingerprint to the address.
checkSeveral: The check of the device runs when you have one PiKVM connection, because a check from this page cannot tell which one you mean. In a chat, enable the connections in the Tools menu.
noAddress: No address: this connection reaches nothing.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.message: Your chats can no longer reach this device, and the user and password saved with it are deleted. To set it up again you must enter them again.

check.title: Check of {{name}}
check.refused: The PiKVM refused this user name or password. If 2FA is on for the device, it is not supported.
check.certificate: The certificate is not trusted. Pin its fingerprint in the address.
check.failed: The check did not finish. Check the address and try again in a moment.

setup.title: How to set it up
setup.step1: On the PiKVM, add a dedicated user (rw, then kvmd-htpasswd add <name>, then ro). The PiKVM has no per-user rights, so this user can do everything: its use is that you can remove it on its own.
setup.step2: Write the address you use to open the PiKVM, plus the pin of its self-signed certificate: https://pikvm.local#sha256=<fingerprint>.
setup.step3: Type the user name and password here. They are sealed together and never shown again.
setup.step4: Leave the write mode on Read only until you have read the limits on this page. Then switch on typing or hard power actions only for the devices that need them.
setup.tls: Get the fingerprint with: openssl s_client -connect pikvm.local:443 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256. The add-on then accepts that one certificate for that one address and never turns verification off.
setup.twofa: A PiKVM with two-factor login (2FA) turned on is not supported in this version, because the one-time code changes every 30 seconds. Turn 2FA off for this device, or leave it out.

writeMode.label: What the agent may do with this device
writeMode.hint: Reading the state is always allowed. Every action is confirmed by you, whatever you choose.

line.propose: Each action waits for your OK.

note.off: Write access is off: this connection only reads the state.
note.propose: Each power action, text and key press waits in your approvals until you confirm it. Typing and hard power actions also need the switch below.

settings.title: Typing and hard power actions
settings.loadFailed: The switches could not be loaded.
settings.saveFailed: The switches could not be saved.
settings.intro: These switches are kept for each device and apply to every user of this server. They are off until an administrator changes them.
settings.physical: A power action can lose unsaved work. Typing and key presses go to whatever has the focus on the machine: a shell, a BIOS menu, a login screen. A person confirms each one and sees the exact text or keys.
settings.readOnly: Only an administrator can change these switches.
settings.broken: The saved switches could not be read, so everything is treated as off. Save them again to repair them.
settings.none: Add a PiKVM connection to set its switches.
settings.typingHint: Lets a chat ask to type text and press keys. Each request still waits for your confirmation.
settings.maxCharsHint: Characters in one typed text. Default {{default}}, at most 1000.
settings.maxCharsShape: Enter a whole number from 1 to 1000.
settings.hardHint: Lets a chat ask for a forced power off, a hardware reset or a long press of the power button. Each request still waits for your confirmation.
settings.saved: Saved. The next call uses the new switches.
settings.never: No screen capture, no disk images, no GPIO, no mouse, and no change to the users or the settings of the device. The add-on refuses text that looks like a private key, a token or a list of passwords.
settings.keys: Keys a chat may press: {{keys}}. No Windows or Meta chords.

approval.physical: This acts on a real machine as soon as you confirm.
approval.asFirst: The first connection that lists this address
approval.asUnknown: A PiKVM connection for this address
approval.hard: This is a hard action: unsaved work is lost.
approval.typeEffect: The text is typed on the keyboard of the machine, into whatever has the focus. A newline presses Enter.
approval.keysEffect: The keys are pressed in this order on the keyboard of the machine.
